components.name: Server Core
components.summary: Main server lifecycle: main(), initServer, serverCron, beforeSleep, and the processCommand/call dispatch path.
components.description: Owns the redis-server process lifecycle and global state (struct redisServer server): main() -> initServerConfig/initServer/initListeners -> aeMain(server.el). serverCron (driven by 'hz', run_with_period macro) handles clientsCron, replicationCron, child-info collection and stats; beforeSleep/afterSleep flush AOF, drain TLS/compression pending data, handle blocked clients and pending writes each event-loop cycle, with a reduced re-entrant path guarded by ProcessingEventsWhileBlocked (processEventsWhileBlocked during RDB/AOF load). Command execution flows preprocessCommand -> processCommand -> call(); searchable as 'command dispatch', 'server cron', 'beforeSleep', 'event loop cycle', 'main loop stall'. Related directives: hz, dynamic-hz; failure symptoms: latency spikes when cron tasks or beforeSleep work (AOF fsync, expired-key cycles) run long.

components.name: Event Loop (ae)
components.summary: Self-contained event-driven library multiplexing socket I/O and timers; aeMain/aeProcessEvents drive everything.
components.description: Minimal event library (originally written for the Jim Tcl interpreter) providing aeEventLoop with file events (aeFileEvent/aeFiredEvent) and timer events; aeCreateEventLoop, aeCreateFileEvent, aeCreateTimeEvent, aeProcessEvents, aeMain, plus aeSetBeforeSleepProc/aeSetAfterSleepProc hooks used by server-core and by each IO thread. The multiplexing backend is chosen at compile time by #ifdef in performance order: evport > epoll > kqueue > select (ae_evport.c/ae_epoll.c/ae_kqueue.c/ae_select.c are #included, not linked). Searchable as 'event loop', 'multiplexing backend', 'aeApiPoll', 'timer resolution', 'busy loop'; uses monotonic clock (monotonicInit).

components.name: Client Networking
components.summary: Client lifecycle, RESP request parsing, reply construction, and output-buffer management (networking.c).
components.description: Implements createClient/freeClient, readQueryFromClient -> processInputBuffer -> processMultibulkBuffer/processInlineBuffer (RESP vs inline protocol), and the reply path: addReply into a fixed c->buf (PROTO_REPLY_CHUNK_BYTES) that overflows into a reply block list, drained by writeToClient/handleClientsWithPendingWrites (with _writeToClientSlave/_writeToClientNonSlave split and an IO-thread variant for replicas). closeClientOnOutputBufferLimitReached enforces client-output-buffer-limit; helloCommand switches clients between RESP2/RESP3 (c->resp) and addReplyPushLen emits RESP3 push frames. Searchable as 'client output buffer', 'obuf limit', 'pending writes', 'protocol error', 'query buffer', 'CLIENT KILL'; directives: client-output-buffer-limit, maxmemory-clients, proto-max-bulk-len, tcp-keepalive.

components.name: Connection Abstraction Layer
components.summary: ConnectionType vtable abstracting TCP/Unix/TLS transports over anet.c low-level socket helpers.
components.description: connection.c/h define the ConnectionType function table (ae_handler, accept_handler, read/write/writev, listen, addr) and connTypeRegister; socket.c registers CT_Socket (tcp), unix.c registers CT_Unix, tls.c registers CT_TLS, so networking code is transport-agnostic. Connection state machine CONN_STATE_CONNECTING/ACCEPTING/CONNECTED/CLOSED plus CONN_FLAG_WRITE_BARRIER; anet.c ('basic TCP socket stuff made a bit less boring') provides anetTcpServer, anetUnixServer, anetNonBlock, keepalive and DNS helpers. Searchable as 'connection type', 'listener', 'accept handler', 'bind', 'unix socket'; directives: port, bind, tcp-backlog, unixsocket, unixsocketperm; symptoms: 'Could not create server TCP listening socket', accept backlog overflow.

components.name: TLS Layer
components.summary: OpenSSL-backed CT_TLS connection type; can be built into the core or as a separate module.
components.description: Implements the CT_TLS ConnectionType over OpenSSL: createSSLContext builds server/client SSL_CTX (redis_tls_ctx/redis_tls_client_ctx) from redisTLSContextConfig, with session caching, keyfile-password callbacks, and TLSv1.3 detection; compiled in-core or as a module depending on USE_OPENSSL/BUILD_TLS_MODULE. Because TLS can buffer decrypted bytes, beforeSleep calls connTypeProcessPendingData/connTypeHasPendingData to drain pending reads and avoid sleeping on hidden data. Searchable as 'TLS handshake failure', 'certificate reload', 'tls-port', 'SSL_ERROR'; directives: tls-port, tls-cert-file, tls-key-file, tls-ciphers, tls-auth-clients, tls-replication, tls-cluster.

components.name: IO Threads
components.summary: Multi-threaded I/O: per-thread event loops offload socket reads, RESP parsing, and writes; commands still run on the main thread.
components.description: iothread.c (2024 redesign) gives each IOThread its own aeEventLoop and IOThreadBeforeSleep; clients are pinned via assignClientToIOThread/fetchClientFromIOThread and exchanged through mutex-protected pending lists plus eventNotifier wakeups (enqueuePendingClientsToMainThread, handleClientsFromMainThread). IO threads perform read(2), protocol parsing (CLIENT_IO_PENDING_COMMAND handoff), reply writing and per-client cron, while processClientsFromIOThread executes the parsed commands on the main thread — with prefetchIOThreadCommands batching memory prefetch — so command execution stays single-threaded and race-free. Searchable as 'threaded I/O', 'io-threads', 'client handoff', 'running_tid', 'IO thread pause'; directive: io-threads (immutable, default 1; io-threads-do-reads is now deprecated).

components.name: RESP Reply Parser & CallReply
components.summary: Callback-based RESP2/RESP3 reply parser and the opaque CallReply object used by RM_Call and Lua redis.call().
components.description: resp_parser.c is a callback-driven parser (parseReply with per-type callbacks: array/set/map/attribute/big-number/verbatim) for replies generated by Redis itself — explicitly documented as NOT safe for parsing user input; call_reply.c wraps it in the opaque CallReply struct (REPLY_FLAG_ROOT/PARSED/RESP3) with lazy parsing and nested sub-reply access, consumed by the module API (RM_Call) and Lua scripting. Searchable as 'RESP parser', 'CallReply', 'RM_Call reply', 'RESP3 map/set/attribute', 'reply protocol blob'.

components.name: Command Table
components.summary: Generated redisCommand table: 460 JSON specs compiled into commands.def via MAKE_CMD macros.
components.description: commands.c is a 13-line shim: MAKE_CMD/MAKE_ARG macros expand commands.def (or commands_with_reply_schema.def when LOG_REQ_RES is defined) into the redisCommand/redisCommandArg tables consumed by lookupCommand and COMMAND DOCS/INFO. The .def file is generated by utils/generate-command-code.py from ~460 per-command JSON files in src/commands/ carrying arity, flags, ACL categories, key specs, history and tips; cli_commands.c reuses the same .def for redis-cli. Searchable as 'command table', 'command flags', 'key specs', 'arity', 'commands.def generation', 'unknown command'.

components.name: Config Engine
components.summary: Typed config registry (standardConfig) behind redis.conf parsing and CONFIG GET/SET/REWRITE.
components.description: config.c declares every directive in a static_configs table via createBoolConfig/createIntConfig/createEnumConfig/createStringConfig/createSpecialConfig macros with flags (MODIFIABLE_CONFIG, IMMUTABLE_CONFIG, DEBUG_CONFIG), bounds, defaults and apply/update callbacks (e.g. updateHZ, applyTLSPort); loadServerConfig/loadServerConfigFromString parse redis.conf and stdin, configSetCommand/configGetCommand implement CONFIG SET/GET with glob matching, and rewriteConfigState powers CONFIG REWRITE preserving user comments; a deprecatedConfig list silently accepts retired directives like io-threads-do-reads. Searchable as 'config directive', 'CONFIG REWRITE', 'immutable config', 'FATAL CONFIG FILE ERROR', 'unknown directive'.

components.name: Background I/O (bio)
components.summary: Dedicated worker threads for blocking ops: deferred close(2), AOF fsync, lazy-free; plus fork-child info pipe.
components.description: bio.c runs fixed worker threads (BIO_WORKER_CLOSE_FILE, BIO_WORKER_AOF_FSYNC, BIO_WORKER_LAZY_FREE) each draining a FIFO job queue in insertion order; bioInit/bioSubmitJob plus bioCreateCloseJob, bioCreateCloseAofJob, bioCreateFsyncJob, bioCreateLazyFreeJob, and completion-callback jobs (bioCreateCompRq / BIO_COMP_RQ_*) that notify the main thread through a pipe read in the event loop; bioDrainWorker/bioKillThreads used at shutdown and by DEBUG. childinfo.c opens a child->parent pipe (openChildInfoPipe) reporting copy-on-write bytes and progress from RDB/AOF fork children, polled by serverCron's receiveChildInfo. Searchable as 'bio threads', 'background fsync', 'lazyfree thread', 'slow close', 'copy-on-write reporting'.

interfaces.name: RESP2/RESP3 Wire Protocol
interfaces.summary: Redis serialization protocol spoken on every client connection; RESP3 adds maps, sets, push and attribute frames.
interfaces.description: The request/reply protocol clients speak over TCP/Unix/TLS: multibulk requests parsed by processMultibulkBuffer, replies built by the addReply* family. HELLO 2|3 (helloCommand) selects the per-client version (c->resp); RESP3 adds typed maps (%), sets (~), doubles, big numbers, verbatim strings, attributes, and out-of-band push frames (addReplyPushLen) used by client-side caching and pub/sub. Same grammar is re-parsed internally by resp_parser.c for RM_Call/Lua replies.

adapters.name: ae epoll backend
adapters.summary: Linux epoll(7) multiplexing backend for the ae event loop (ae_epoll.c), selected when HAVE_EPOLL.
adapters.description: aeApiCreate/aeApiPoll wrappers over epoll_create/epoll_ctl/epoll_wait; the default and fastest general backend on Linux, compiled in via #ifdef HAVE_EPOLL in ae.c.

adapters.name: ae kqueue backend
adapters.summary: BSD/macOS kqueue multiplexing backend (ae_kqueue.c), selected when HAVE_KQUEUE.
adapters.description: aeApi* implementation over kqueue/kevent for FreeBSD, OpenBSD and macOS builds; chosen after evport/epoll in ae.c's compile-time preference order.

adapters.name: ae select backend
adapters.summary: Portable select(2) fallback backend (ae_select.c) used when no better multiplexer exists.
adapters.description: Lowest-performance fallback in ae.c's backend ladder; limited by FD_SETSIZE, used only on platforms without evport/epoll/kqueue.

adapters.name: ae evport backend
adapters.summary: illumos/Solaris event-ports backend (ae_evport.c), highest priority in the compile-time ladder.
adapters.description: Contributed by Joyent for illumos event ports (port_create/port_getn); listed first in ae.c's 'ordered by performances, descending' backend selection.

adapters.name: OpenSSL
adapters.summary: OpenSSL library backing tls.c: SSL_CTX setup, handshakes, session caching, cert/key loading.
adapters.description: tls.c targets OpenSSL >= 1.0 with version-conditional init (OPENSSL_config vs OPENSSL_init_crypto), RAND seeding checks, and locking callbacks for pre-1.1.0; encapsulated so it can ship as a loadable TLS module (BUILD_TLS_MODULE).

config_vars.name: hz
config_vars.description: Controls how often serverCron runs and the granularity of run_with_period tasks (client timeouts, expired-key sampling, replicationCron); updateHZ callback applies changes live. Higher hz = more CPU, lower latency for background tasks.

config_vars.name: dynamic-hz
config_vars.summary: Adapt effective hz to the number of connected clients.
config_vars.description: When enabled, the effective cron frequency scales with client count so clientsCron can visit every client in bounded time without wasting CPU on idle instances.

config_vars.name: io-threads
config_vars.summary: Number of I/O threads (1 = classic single-threaded I/O).
config_vars.description: IMMUTABLE_CONFIG, range 1-128. Above 1, initThreadedIO spawns IOThreadMain threads each with its own event loop, handling reads, RESP parsing and writes; redis.conf advises leaving at least one spare core and enabling only under real CPU pressure.

config_vars.name: client-output-buffer-limit
config_vars.summary: Per-class (normal/replica/pubsub) hard and soft output buffer limits.
config_vars.description: Special multi-arg config enforced by closeClientOnOutputBufferLimitReached: clients exceeding the hard limit, or the soft limit for soft-seconds, are disconnected — the classic cause of 'client scheduled to be closed ASAP for overcoming of output buffer limits' and replica disconnect loops.

config_vars.name: maxmemory-clients
config_vars.summary: Total memory cap across all client buffers (client eviction).
config_vars.description: SSizeT config (bytes or percent of maxmemory); when aggregate client query/output buffers exceed it, Redis evicts the highest-usage clients (applyClientMaxMemoryUsage, memory usage buckets updated by updateClientMemUsageAndBucket).

config_vars.name: tcp-backlog
config_vars.description: IMMUTABLE_CONFIG passed to anetTcpServer; must be raised together with /proc/sys/net/core/somaxconn or bursts of connections get dropped in SYN/accept queues.

config_vars.name: port
config_vars.description: Applied via updatePort which rebuilds the connListener for CT_Socket; distinct from tls-port which drives the CT_TLS listener.

config_vars.name: tls-port
config_vars.description: applyTLSPort creates the CT_TLS listener; requires tls-cert-file/tls-key-file to be configured or connections fail at handshake.

features.name: Threaded I/O
features.summary: Multi-core scaling of socket I/O and protocol parsing without sharding or pipelining.
features.description: Per-thread event loops (iothread.c) take over read(2), RESP parsing and write(2) for assigned clients while command execution remains on the main thread; enabled by io-threads > 1. Redis.conf frames it as an alternative to pipelining/multi-instance sharding for boxes with 4+ cores.

features.name: TLS Connections
features.summary: Encrypted client, replication, and cluster-bus connections via the CT_TLS connection type.
features.description: TLS terminates inside the server through the pluggable connection layer; tls-replication and tls-cluster extend it to replica links and the cluster bus. Buildable in-core or as a module (USE_OPENSSL/BUILD_TLS_MODULE).

decisions.title: Select the I/O multiplexing backend at compile time, ordered by performance
decisions.statement: ae.c #includes exactly one backend (evport > epoll > kqueue > select) chosen by preprocessor checks rather than runtime dispatch.
decisions.rationale: Avoids virtual-dispatch overhead in the hottest loop and keeps each backend a tiny drop-in file implementing the same aeApi* functions.
decisions.description: The ae.c comment 'Include the best multiplexing layer supported by this system. The following should be ordered by performances, descending' documents the explicit ladder: HAVE_EVPORT -> HAVE_EPOLL -> HAVE_KQUEUE -> select fallback.
decisions.evidence: src/ae.c lines 30-44: '#ifdef HAVE_EVPORT ... #include "ae_evport.c" ... #include "ae_select.c"' with the ordering comment.

decisions.title: IO threads offload reads, parsing, and writes — never command execution
decisions.statement: IO threads own socket I/O and RESP parsing for their clients; parsed commands are handed to the main thread (processClientsFromIOThread) which alone touches shared server data.
decisions.rationale: Keeps the data plane single-threaded and lock-free for keyspace access while parallelizing the dominant syscall/parse cost; clients marked CLIENT_IO_READ/WRITE_ENABLED are disabled before handoff to avoid races.
decisions.description: iothread.c enforces the boundary with running_tid switching, mutex-guarded pending lists, and asserts that a client is neither readable nor writable in an IO thread while the main thread processes it; redis.conf documents that threads cover 'writes... but also reads and protocol parsing'.
decisions.evidence: redis.conf THREADED I/O section ('we not only use threads for writes... but also use threads for reads and protocol parsing') and src/iothread.c processClientsFromIOThread comment 'The main thread processes the clients from IO threads... IO threads never free client since this operation access much server data.'

decisions.title: Pluggable ConnectionType vtable unifies TCP, Unix, and TLS transports
decisions.statement: All transports register a ConnectionType (function table with ae_handler, accept, read/write/writev, listen) via connTypeRegister, so networking.c is transport-agnostic.
decisions.rationale: Lets TLS ship as an optional module and keeps encryption/socket details out of client logic; the same abstraction supports replication and cluster links over any transport.
decisions.description: connection.h defines the ConnectionType struct with init/cleanup/configure and I/O hooks; socket.c (CT_Socket), unix.c (CT_Unix) and tls.c (CT_TLS) each register themselves into the static connTypes[CONN_TYPE_MAX] array.
decisions.evidence: src/connection.h ConnectionType struct definition; src/connection.c connTypeRegister; CT_Socket/CT_Unix/CT_TLS registrations in src/socket.c:467, src/unix.c:218, src/tls.c:403.

decisions.title: Command table generated from per-command JSON specs
decisions.statement: Command metadata lives in src/commands/*.json (460 files) and is compiled by utils/generate-command-code.py into commands.def, expanded by MAKE_CMD macros in commands.c.
decisions.rationale: Single source of truth for arity, flags, ACL categories, key specs, history and docs shared by the server, COMMAND DOCS output, and redis-cli (cli_commands.c includes the same .def).
decisions.description: commands.c is a 13-line macro shim; a parallel commands_with_reply_schema.def exists for LOG_REQ_RES builds that validate reply schemas.
decisions.evidence: src/commands.c (#include "commands.def" behind MAKE_CMD/MAKE_ARG), src/commands/ JSON directory, utils/generate-command-code.py.

decisions.title: Internal RESP parser is deliberately not hardened for user input
decisions.statement: resp_parser.c only parses replies generated by Redis itself (RM_Call, Lua redis.call) and skips validations, trading safety checks for speed.
decisions.rationale: The blob being parsed was just produced by the reply-writing code, so full protocol validation would be redundant on the hot module/scripting path.
decisions.description: Header comment states: 'NOTE: This parser is designed to only handle replies generated by Redis itself. It does not perform many required validations and thus NOT SAFE FOR PARSING USER INPUT.'

documents.title: redis.conf annotated configuration reference
documents.summary: Self-documenting example config; the THREADED I/O, TLS, and clients sections explain tuning rationale.
documents.description: The shipped redis.conf doubles as the operator manual for core-runtime directives: it explains when to enable io-threads (4+ cores, leave a spare), client-output-buffer-limit classes, TLS setup, and hz/dynamic-hz tradeoffs, and is kept in sync with config.c defaults.
